target: One preemptive machine must run three independent recurring jobs. Their (execution time C, period T, relative deadline D) triples are (1,5,3), (2,6,2), and (4,15,8). Releases recur forever with each job's first release at time 0. A capacity dashboard reports total utilization 0.8. The team must determine whether earliest-deadline-first can meet every deadline on this single machine, including any short-interval overload.
surface: A previous factory scheduling review admitted recurring jobs whenever total average utilization stayed below one. It calculated the sum of execution-time/period ratios and declared a schedule with utilization 0.8 feasible because 20% average capacity remained.
structural: An avionics admission test for preemptive uniprocessor EDF used the processor demand bound. For each task i, its demand in an interval t was dbf_i(t)=max(0, floor((t-D_i)/T_i)+1)*C_i. The task set was feasible only if the sum of these demands was at most t at every relevant absolute-deadline candidate; one violating interval was a certificate of infeasibility.
rubric: Explicitly selects the EDF processor demand-bound feasibility criterion, not utilization alone.
Evaluates the demand bound at t=8 using the supplied (C,T,D) triples.
Computes demands 2, 4, and 4 at t=8, totaling 10 units.
Concludes 10>8 is an overload certificate and the recurring job set is infeasible under EDF despite utilization 0.8.
States the preemptive independent-task/synchronous-release model or that all relevant deadline candidates normally require checking.
